sections.thesis: Treasury yields fell as investors weighed Democrats' big midterm wins and lower oil prices.

sentences.text: Treasury yields fell as investors weighed Democrats' big midterm wins and lower oil prices.
The 10-year yield fell to 4.891% from 4.951% and the two-year to 4.579%, its lowest since early September.
Derivative markets priced inflation one year out at around 2.1%, down from 2.4% on Tuesday.
Friday's payrolls report is the key near-term catalyst.

sections.thesis: The dollar fell as Democrats' control of both houses of Congress raised the risk of political gridlock.

sentences.text: The dollar fell as Democrats' control of both houses of Congress raised the risk of political gridlock.
The US Dollar Index traded around 101.45, down 0.40% on the day, after a low of 101.21, its weakest since September 30.
Resilient US data helped it regain some ground.
ING said on Wednesday the dollar could see a little more weakness into 2027.

sections.thesis: Wall Street had its biggest daily gain in months as investors bet the Democrats' win could restrain White House policymaking.

sentences.text: Wall Street had its biggest daily gain in months as investors bet the Democrats' win could restrain White House policymaking.
The S&P 500 closed 1.6% higher, its biggest one-day jump since early August, while the Nasdaq 100 added 0.9%.
Amazon and Microsoft jumped 6.1% and 6.7% on bets that established tech is less exposed to pushback on new data centres, while CoreWeave fell 9.9%.

sections.thesis: Oil fell to its lowest in two months as the Democrats' landslide raised pressure on Donald Trump to end his war in Iran.

sentences.text: Oil fell to its lowest in two months as the Democrats' landslide raised pressure on Donald Trump to end his war in Iran.
Brent settled 8.7% lower at $94.62 a barrel.
US diesel inventories fell below 100mn barrels for the first time in more than two decades.
Gold rose over 3.60% to near $4,065 as the weaker dollar boosted its appeal.
